idiom_name: case class MonsterType descriptor + Map registry; enum/sealed for the closed case
implementation_notes: A final case class is Scala's canonical immutable data carrier - one declaration gives structural equality, copy and extractors - so the type object is a case-class instance and the typed object is an ordinary class holding a reference to it. The registry is a Map[String, MonsterType] built once from JSON or config, and per-type behaviour is a function value (Monster => String) or a Strategy type stored in the descriptor rather than a subclass. Where the set of kinds is closed, enum/sealed hierarchies with exhaustive matching are the compile-checked alternative (Scala 3 enums desugar to exactly that), which is why the data-shaped descriptor is the idiomatic form here and the classic TypeClass/Class pair is not needed. Reconciliation of descriptor identity goes through the id: case-class equality is structural.
pitfalls: Case-class equality is structural: two descriptors with the same fields are equal, so registry/map membership must be keyed by id, not by the descriptor.

The generated copy is shallow - a List/Map field is shared with the derived descriptor - so 'tuning' a variant that holds collections can mutate its base unless the collections are immutable (Scala's default List/Map are, Array and mutable.* are not).
A var in the case class (rather than in the typed object) participates in equality and makes a shared descriptor mutable; keep instance state in Monster.
